metadata.title: How to Stuff a Thanksgiving Turkey| Williams-Sonoma
metadata.description:
A happy Thanksgiving holiday is simply incomplete without a yummy turkey dinner! In this video from Williams-Sonoma, you can watch the steps on how to cook a turkey with Williams Sonoma Culinary Expert, Amanda. When stuffing a turkey, you need to remember that you need to allow an extra 30-60 minutes for the turkey and the stuffing to roast. Also, don't brine it if you want to stuff it.

The turkey and the stuffing ingredients should be at room temperature for an hour before you begin cooking. For stuffing a turkey, line the turkey cavity with a cheese cloth. Tuck it such that the ends of the cheesecloth are still outside of the turkey. Now, add the stuffing in this cloth pouch. Leave a lot of space since the juices will fill in the cavities during the roasting process. 

Secure the cloth and the cavity opening with trussing needles. Tie these up with a piece of twine. Fold the legs and tie up with twine. After roasting and seasoning in the oven, the turkey looks gloriously golden-brown. Make sure the temperature of the stuffing has reached 165 F. Then, let it rest for 20 minutes before removing the stuffing. The stuffing can then be served up in your best china.

Now that you know a little more about how to cook a turkey, you can impress your friends and family with a fabulous Thanksgiving dinner!

To explore further, visit our Williams-Sonoma website:  http://www.williams-sonoma.com/

Get free stuffing recipes at the Williams-Sonoma website:  http://www.williams-sonoma.com/search/results.html?words=turkey+stuffing&activeTab=recipes&page=1 

For savory stuffing visit: http://www.williams-sonoma.com/recipe/tip/savory-stuffings.html

nodes.plm_caption: The video shows a woman demonstrating how to cook a turkey, including the preparation of the turkey, stuffing it with ingredients, and placing it in an oven. The woman is seen speaking at the beginning of the video. The video ends with a clip of the completed roasted turkey. The video is set in a kitchen with various food items seen behind the woman, including bread and onions in a bowl. The video is shot in a well-lit and modern-looking kitchen with a wooden surface under the roasting tray.

summary.brief: A woman lines a turkey’s cavity with cheesecloth, loosely stuffs it, trusses the bird, roasts it, checks the stuffing temperature, rests the turkey, and serves the fragrant stuffing.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the woman reminding viewers to bring both the turkey and the stuffing to room temperature. She folds a piece of cheesecloth in half, lines the turkey’s cavity with it and leaves the ends hanging outside. Loose stuffing is spooned into the cloth‑lined cavity, leaving plenty of room for expansion and for the turkey’s juices to be absorbed. After tucking the cloth ends back into the bird, she inserts two trussing needles, adds two more, and threads kitchen twine through them, lacing and double‑tying the twine to secure the cavity, then tucks the wings under and folds and ties the legs. The seasoned turkey is placed in a roasting pan and roasted. When done, she inserts an instant‑read thermometer through the cheesecloth to verify that the stuffing has reached 165 °F, tents the bird with foil, and lets it rest for 20 minutes. Finally she pulls out the cheesecloth, removes the stuffing as a single package, transfers it to a serving dish, and shows its fragrant, moist appearance.

action.detailed: Stuff the turkey by lining its cavity with folded cheesecloth, spooning in loose stuffing, then secure the cloth and close the cavity with trussing needles and kitchen twine.
action.actor: the woman in a white apron and green shirt

summary.brief: The woman stuffs a turkey using a cheesecloth pouch, trusses it with twine, roasts it, checks temperatures, rests it, and serves the stuffing.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with the woman folding a piece of cheesecloth in half and tucking it into the turkey cavity, leaving the ends outside. She loosely spoons the prepared stuffing into the cloth, then inserts two trussing needles and adds two more, lacing kitchen twine around the needles like a shoe‑lace and tying a double knot to seal the cavity. After tucking the wings under, she folds and ties the legs with additional twine, seasons the bird, and places it in a roasting pan to roast. When the bird is done, she inserts an instant‑read thermometer through the cheesecloth to confirm the stuffing has reached 165 °F, then tents the turkey with foil and lets it rest for twenty minutes. She removes the cheesecloth, allowing the hot stuffing to fall into a serving dish, checks the turkey’s internal temperature with a thermometer, and finally presents the fragrant, moist stuffing alongside the roasted turkey.
